To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumption of XOS or inulin-XOS results in beneficial changes in the intestinal environment of healthy subjects on a high-fat Western diet.
XOS in combination, but not alone, modulates the intestinal environment, decreases endotoxaemia and attenuates the pro-inflammatory effects of a high fat diet in the blood.
consumption of XOS or inulin-XOS mixture in combination with a high-fat diet modulates the intestinal environment and attenuates the pro-inflammatory effects of LPS in the blood of the subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new prebiotics and with the identification of their mechanisms of action in the intestinal microbiota.
the development of novel functional foods with health-promoting properties.
the effects of prebiotic oligofructose-enriched inulin (OF-IN) and xylo-oligo-saccharide (XS) on gut microbiota, endotoxemia (lipopolysisaccharides, LPS) and immune parameters in healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of inulin and XOS is a more beneficial prebiotic than the single compounds, but that the single compounds have their own beneficial effects.
the combination of XOS and inulin is more effective in modulating the gut environment and immune system than XOS alone.
XOS in combination inulin has beneficial effects on the intestinal microbiota, the intestinal environment, the intestinal immunity and the blood of healthy individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consumption of XOS or INU-XOS in combination with a high-fat diet may be beneficial in reducing the risk of chronic diseases associated with high-fat diets.
XOS alone or with inulin may be used as prebiotics to improve the health of the gut and the host.
XOS alone and XOS in combination inulin have prebiotic properties and that the latter also has immune-modulating properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prebiotic properties of XOS are not only limited to the modulation of the intestinal microbiota but also extend to a modulation of the intestinal environment, as well as the immune status.
the prebiotic effects of XOS are not only limited to the gut, but also extend to the blood.
XOS in combination is more than the sum of its parts.
